1. SURFACE: ISO 8601 dates (YYYY-MM-DD), decimal amounts, USD-like plain numbers, ambiguous whether MM or DD is 3rd field—but ISO puts year first so format read as year-month-day unambiguous on surface.

2. CONTENT: Check values — month field max seen "04", "01", "12" — all ≤12, consistent w/ ISO. Day field "03","05","01","09","02" — all ≤12 too, so day-vs-month swap theoretically possible from digits alone. But header explicit "date" + ISO YYYY-MM-DD is de facto standard (RFC 3339), no locale field order ambiguity like MM/DD/YYYY vs DD/MM/YYYY. Content matches surface — genuine ISO order, not spreadsheet-locale swap.
CONTENT VERDICT: NO MISMATCH

3. MISREADINGS:
- Misreading: treat as US-style MM/DD/YYYY parsing logic mistakenly applied to YYYY-MM-DD string (e.g. manual string split assuming wrong field order) → could swap month/day silently since both ≤12 in sample. Evidence against: ISO 8601 fixes order as year-month-day; no row has day>12 to catch bug, so validate parser uses proper ISO parse (datetime.strptime %Y-%m-%d), not manual guess.
- Misreading: "April 2026" task filter implemented as string prefix match `"2026-04"` vs. parsing date obj and checking month==4 & year==2026 — both work here since data ISO, but if any row had non-ISO format mixed in, prefix match breaks silently. No such row in sample though.
- Misreading: amount field assumed locale decimal comma (European) — surface shows "." decimal, standard. No mismatch: all values plain float w/ period decimal, consistent.
- Misreading: timezone assumption — date-only field, no time/offset given. Risk: transaction near month boundary (e.g. 2026-04-01) could shift day if timezone conversion applied. No time component present, so no tz conversion needed — treat as naive local date.
